question:
Africa could be labeled the supplier of mostly unprocessed products to the rest of the world. The crystal fear that the continent is left behind in its development efforts to provide the same for the rest of the globe. One cannot deny that Africa still has untapped natural resources and human resources even after the long and bloody experience of slaves and colonialism. It is arguable whether or not Africa can be characterized as a high continental trade integration. Such a move, according to many commentators, is believed to help the continent to take the place it deserves.

2

Needless to say, continents apart from Africa, especially those in the northern hemisphere, have developed a special type of system that unites one another and fosters their development in every aspect. These could not have achieved what the rest of the continents have accomplished. It is undeniable that Africa has sacrificed its opportunities for the sake of the rest to prosper uninterruptedly. It was a good clear way to rectify the course of the system. African nations have designed special strategies to achieve their vision to create Africa we want through the Agenda 2030 and Agenda 2063 of the African Union. In this long-term agenda, African nations, through their leaders have signed multiple agreements to meet the desired goals.

3

Some of the notable measures that followed those multiple agreements are the points of focus of this paragraph. In this respect, continental Africa has taken tangible actions to circumvent the challenges arising from the stereotyped way of doing trade including the adoption of an action plan for the implementation of the continental trade. The trade agreement, when operationalized, will liberalize trade in goods. It is also expected to liberalize trade in services gradually and open the door for the elimination of 90% of tariffs in goods. It is also expected to liberate trade in services.

4

Moreover, in recent years, regional economic partnerships have been strengthened. Accordingly, the Tripartite Free Trade Area which incorporates EAC, COMESA, and SADC was regionally economic partnership endorsed in June 2015 in Sharm-el-Sheikh, Egypt with the aim of fostering integration and helping member states to circumvent the challenges arising from overlapping memberships. As of July 2022, there were 22 signatories to the Tripartite Free Trade Area Agreement. The 29 states of the three regional communities and 11 states had ratified it. Three additional ratifications are required to operationalize the Tripartite Free Trade Area.

5

To achieve what has been planned and see the Africa we want, every stakeholder group as well as the wider society must work for the intended goals. Organizations such as the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA) confirmed that it will provide technical support and other necessary analysis in order to enhance the initiatives mentioned above.

question: The author's main purpose is to:
options: A. call the attention of the reader that Africa is a continent with abundant yet untapped resources.
B. refute the claims of regional organizations like COMESA, EAC, and SADC.

C. argue in favor of the idea that the Africa we all dream to see can be appreciated through efforts exerted by some regional organizations like COMESA, EAC and SADC in fostering economic integration.
D. warn that Africa is not yet ready for economic integration.

question: The title **The Africa We Want** implies
options: A. we can turn Africa into a tourist haven.
B. there are few desirable things about Africa.
C. If every stake holder works for a better Africa, we can make the dream come true.
D. Africa we want.

question: In paragraph 4, the writer says, "Africa is a global trader, but of mostly **unprocessed** products." Which word do you think best describes the state of Africa in the global economy?
options: A. poor
B. destitute
C. isolated
D. conservative

question: In the last paragraph of the passage the writer says, "**to achieve what has been planned and see the 'Africa we want', every stake holder, coupled with following statements would the above quotation most likely support?**"
options: A. Stake holders are working closely with the people of Africa
B. The writer thinks the Africa he wants will materialize sooner than later.
C. A concerted effort from all concerned bodies is mandatory if Africa is to develop as desired.
D. Africa has embarked in integrated development.
explanation: The phrase 'every stake holder, coupled with...' strongly implies that universal participation or a **concerted effort from all concerned bodies** is required to realize the vision ('the Africa we want'). Therefore, Option C best supports the idea of mandatory widespread effort.

question: The underlined word 'circumvent' in the fourth paragraph most nearly means
options: beat
win
ignore
abandon
explanation: In context, 'circumvent' means to avoid or beat a challenge by finding a way around it.

question: In paragraph 4, what expression has the writer used to show that he wants to add a point or information to what he has said in paragraph 3?
options: furthermore
moreover
in addition
hence
explanation: The writer uses the expression 'moreover' in paragraph 4 to add additional information to what was stated earlier.

question: In Paragraph 1, line 6, the phrase 'such a move' refers to
options: the integration of the Africa we want through multi-lateral trade with all the continents
continentalization of Africa
the fact that Africa still has untapped natural resources and human resources even after the long and bloody experience of civilization
Africa as the supplier of mostly unprocessed products to the world
explanation: 'Such a move' refers to the action believed to help Africa take its deserved place, which is the integration of Africa through intra-continental trade.

question: The term 'intra-continental trade' implies
options: a trade that should prevail between and among African countries
a trade that should take place between continents including those in northern hemisphere and Africa
a trade that should take place between Africa and other continents
a network of trading that should exist between two countries of Africa
explanation: ‘Intra-continental trade’ means trade happening within the same continent—here referring to trade among African countries.

question: In paragraph 2 the phrase 'These continents' refers to
options: all continents including Africa
the northern continents apart from Africa
all continents excluding Africa
all continents including those in the northern hemisphere
explanation: The paragraph contrasts Africa with the northern hemisphere continents, so 'These continents' refers to the northern continents apart from Africa.
